title: Touch Control Error
shortDescription: The cooktop detected a stuck or shorted touch key.
fullDescription:
C-E1 is displayed when the touch control module registers continuous activation of a key for longer than 30 seconds. Water, cookware, or a spill on the glass may bridge the capacitive sensors.

Removing the item and wiping the glass usually clears the fault. Persistent C-E1 after cleaning indicates a failing touch board.

causes.cause: Water or spill on touch area

fixSteps.title: Clear the glass
fixSteps.instruction: Remove cookware and wipe the touch area dry with a microfiber cloth.

fixSteps.title: Reset power
fixSteps.instruction: Switch off the cooktop breaker for 60 seconds and switch back on.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if C-E1 returns after cleaning, since replacing the touch board requires removing the glass top.
videoSearchQuery: Samsung cooktop C-E1 touch error fix

faq.a: No, C-E1 locks all burners until cleared.

title: Over-Temperature Shutdown
shortDescription: A cooking zone exceeded its maximum safe surface temperature.
fullDescription:
Samsung cooktops display C-E2 when the glass sensor reads above roughly 530C. The affected zone is disabled until it cools down.

Common triggers are empty pans on high heat, warped cookware that does not dissipate heat, or a failing glass NTC sensor.

fixSteps.title: Let cooktop cool
fixSteps.instruction: Allow the glass to cool completely before retrying the zone.

fixSteps.title: Use flat cookware
fixSteps.instruction: Check pan bottom is flat with a straight edge. Replace warped pans.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if C-E2 recurs with flat cookware and a cool glass.

faq.a: Unlikely. The sensor shuts it off before damage occurs.

title: Temperature Sensor Error
shortDescription: The surface temperature sensor for a cooking zone is faulty.
fullDescription:
Error C-E3 means the control board sees an open or shorted NTC sensor on one of the cooking zones. The zone is disabled to prevent over-heating.

The sensors sit directly under the glass and are rarely serviceable without lifting the glass top.

fixSteps.title: Identify affected zone
fixSteps.instruction: Note which burner triggers the code so technician can target the sensor.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Lifting the glass top is required. Follow service manual to detach and replace the NTC sensor.

whenToCallPro: Most homeowners should call a pro since damaging the glass top during disassembly is expensive.

faq.q: Can other zones still be used?
faq.a: Typically yes, only the affected zone is locked.

title: Induction Coil Communication Error
shortDescription: The induction generator reports a communication failure with the main board.
fullDescription:
CE-E2 on induction models indicates the inverter coil module is not responding on the internal bus. The cooktop disables induction output.

Typical causes include a loose 4-pin data connector between boards, or a damaged inverter assembly after a voltage spike.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Switch off breaker for 2 minutes and restore.

fixSteps.title: Reseat inverter harness
fixSteps.instruction: Drop the cooktop from the counter, unplug and reconnect the coil data harness.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if reseating does not resolve CE-E2, since inverter replacement requires careful cable routing and grounding.

faq.q: Does this mean my cookware is bad?
faq.a: No, CE-E2 is a board-level error, not a cookware detection error.

title: Cooling Fan Error
shortDescription: The internal cooling fan for the induction module is not spinning.
fullDescription:
ER-21 appears when the cooktop's cooling fan tachometer is silent. The fan protects the inverter and coils from overheating during cooking.

Dust clogging the intake or a failed fan motor are the main causes. Without cooling the cooktop derates or shuts off entirely.

fixSteps.title: Vacuum vents
fixSteps.instruction: Clean the intake under the cooktop and any exhaust slots on the counter edge.

fixSteps.title: Replace fan
fixSteps.instruction: Drop the cooktop, unplug the fan connector, install a new fan and refit.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the cooktop is recessed in solid surface where removal is tricky.

faq.a: Induction electronics run hot and fail quickly without airflow.

title: Inverter Overheat
shortDescription: The inverter heatsink has reached its thermal limit.
fullDescription:
ER-22 is triggered when the heatsink NTC on the inverter reads above safe limits. The cooktop reduces power or stops output until temperatures drop.

Blocked ventilation, failed cooling fan, or thermal grease degradation on older units are typical causes.

fixSteps.title: Cool down and clean
fixSteps.instruction: Allow unit to cool. Vacuum dust from intake and exhaust.

fixSteps.title: Check fan operation
fixSteps.instruction: After restart, verify fan spins audibly. Replace if quiet.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if ventilation is clear and the fan runs, since the inverter may need replacement.

faq.q: Can I just keep cooking at lower power?
faq.a: Short term yes, but repeated overheats shorten inverter life.

title: Line Voltage Out of Range
shortDescription: Supply voltage is below or above the safe operating window.
fullDescription:
ER-31 indicates the cooktop sees less than approximately 180V or more than 260V on 240V models. The unit refuses to start to protect the inverter.

Low voltage is common on long branch circuits under load, while high voltage can indicate a utility or neutral issue.

fixSteps.title: Measure voltage
fixSteps.instruction: With cooktop off, measure outlet line-to-line voltage. Expect 220-245V.

fixSteps.title: Call electrician
fixSteps.instruction: If voltage is out of range, stop using and arrange an electrician visit.

whenToCallPro: Always call an electrician for out-of-range voltage. Do not repeatedly reset the cooktop.

faq.a: Possibly, which is why the protection trips.

title: Relay Stuck Error
shortDescription: A power relay on the main board is stuck closed.
fullDescription:
ER-41 is flagged when the controller commands a relay off but still senses current flow. A welded relay risks uncommanded heating.

The only proper repair is main board replacement.

fixSteps.title: Stop use
fixSteps.instruction: Shut off breaker immediately. Do not keep cooking with ER-41.

fixSteps.title: Schedule service
fixSteps.instruction: Arrange board replacement by a Samsung technician.

whenToCallPro: Always. Do not DIY repair a welded relay.

faq.a: Potentially. Keep the cooktop de-energized until repaired.

title: EEPROM Memory Error
shortDescription: The main control board failed its self-check.
fullDescription:
ER-51 means the EEPROM containing calibration and settings is corrupt. The cooktop may still boot but will not save settings.

Unless a service tech can reflash the board, replacement is the standard fix.

fixSteps.title: Try factory reset
fixSteps.instruction: Hold the power key for 20 seconds at breaker-on to attempt a memory rewrite.

fixSteps.title: Replace board
fixSteps.instruction: If reset fails, schedule a main board replacement.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro for board swap and calibration.

faq.a: Occasionally. If not, the board is failing.

title: No Pan Detected
shortDescription: Induction zone cannot detect compatible cookware.
fullDescription:
F0 is an informational code meaning the induction zone energised briefly and found no ferrous cookware. The zone then idles at low power.

This is not a fault as long as it clears when you place a compatible pan on the zone.

fixSteps.title: Test magnet
fixSteps.instruction: A fridge magnet should stick to the pan bottom. If not, the pan is not induction compatible.

fixSteps.title: Center larger pan
fixSteps.instruction: Use a pan at least as large as the zone's minimum diameter.

whenToCallPro: Not required.
videoSearchQuery: Samsung induction cooktop F0 pan detect

faq.q: Why do some pans not work?
faq.a: Aluminum and copper without magnetic base will not couple to induction.

title: Child Lock Active
shortDescription: Controls are disabled because child lock is engaged.
fullDescription:
L on the display means the child lock has been engaged intentionally or accidentally. Cooktop will not respond until unlocked.

Hold the key icon for 3 seconds to toggle the lock.

fixSteps.title: Disable lock
fixSteps.instruction: Hold the lock key until L disappears and a confirmation tone plays.

whenToCallPro: Never.

faq.a: Usually from accidental long-press during cleaning.

title: Residual Heat Indicator
shortDescription: The glass is still hot after use.
fullDescription:
H is a safety indicator, not an error. It stays lit as long as the glass surface remains above roughly 60C.

It will clear automatically once the zone cools.

fixSteps.title: Allow to cool
fixSteps.instruction: Do not touch the zone until H clears.

whenToCallPro: Never.

faq.q: Is the cooktop broken if H stays on?
faq.a: Only if it remains after several hours with no cooking, which points to a sensor fault.
